In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the control of gene expression in the early embryo of the fruit fly, Drosophila melanogaster.
the molecular mechanisms that underly the formation of the body plan in the fruitfly, Drosophila melanogaster.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Bicoid gradient provides positional information along the anterior–posterior axis of the embryo.

the h7‐element, by sensing region‐ and time‐specific combinations of transcriptional factors, mediates position‐ and time‐dependent gene expression in a manner that is consistent with the known embryonic patterning processes.

the h7‐element, by virtue of its modular design and its ability to sense region‐specific combinations of activators and repressors, provides a paradigmatic example of a cis‐regulatory element that mediates position‐specific gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the minimal enhancer elements for the most posterior h7 stripe, and that we have shown that Bicoid and caudal function together as redundant activators in the h7 stripe.

the posterior determinant Caudal and the anterior determinant Bicooid act as redundant activators of h stripe 6 expression, whereas Caudal and a combination of gap gene products act as repressors to limit the expression domain of h stripe 5.

the h7‐element provides an excellent example of the modular organization of a cis‐regulatory element that mediates the complex control of a pair‐rule gene by a variety of factors, including the maternal and zygotic homeodomain proteins Bicoid, Caudal, and Krüppel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the h7 element, which is part of the modular enhancer that mediates h stripe 7, is sufficient for position‐dependent gene regulation in the posterior region.
the h7‐element is a modular array of binding sites that mediates the position‐dependent activation of the h gene.

the h7‐element, which mediates the position‐dependent expression of the most posterior segmental gene, h, is activated by a combinatorial mechanism involving both Bicoid and the posterior determinant Caudal, which form complementary concentration gradients along the anterior–posterior (A–P) axis of the embryo (Figure 1).
